summary: Light on a small island at the south entrance to Grand Passage, Bay of Fundy: lit 1850, rebuilt 1909, decommissioned 2014, restored by volunteers in 2025.

structures.note: square skeleton tower carrying the current Coast Guard light

access.note: Reached by boat (NSLPS). LighthouseFriends visitor note: grounds open, tower closed; a view of the light from South Point, Brier Island.

facts.agency: Municipality of the District of Digby
facts.ownership_note: NSLPS: owned by the Municipality of the District of Digby. LighthouseFriends visitor note: owned by the Canadian Coast Guard; its history says divestiture is a multi-year process. SaltWire 2025: the municipality took ownership in 2023.

corrections.why: The record's position is from OpenStreetMap. The Canadian Coast Guard List of Lights gives the light (H3878) at 44 15 25.7 N, 066 20 13.1 W; the proposed value is that entry in decimal degrees. Difference is about 50 m. Reviewer to confirm.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NSLPS and the register give 1850 as the year the light was lit. LighthouseFriends dates the first keeper's hiring to 1851, which is a different event and is not a conflict in the light's date.
The register gives recognition on 14 June 2021; LighthouseFriends says December 2021. The story follows the register's date.
NSLPS lists older characteristics for the 1909 tower (fixed white 1883; flashing yellow 1992). The current entry in the Coast Guard list is LFl G 6s on the skeleton tower, which the record uses.

LighthouseFriends' visitor note names the Canadian Coast Guard as owner; NSLPS lists the Municipality of the District of Digby; LighthouseFriends' history describes divestiture as a multi-year process; SaltWire (2025) says the municipality took ownership in 2023. The story reports all four and does not choose between them.

LighthouseFriends gives a fifth-order Chance lens for the 1909 tower; NSLPS gives a 5th order dioptric lens for 1922 to 1941 and a 4th order lens from 1992. The story reports both and does not reconcile them.

notes_for_editor: Built on LighthouseFriends (facts, and quotations from the 1885 Sailing Directions and the 1857 Condon inspection as LighthouseFriends prints them; the primary Board of Works and Assembly papers were not in the corpus), the register text (Heritage Guide), NSLPS, the Coast Guard List of Lights (H3878), three Canadian Department of Marine reports from the corpus, and the 2025 SaltWire restoration report. CBC's 2025 article timed out and was not read. The SAIL2 site (sail2.ca) has an expired certificate and was not read. Wikipedia used for leads only. Keeper roster is LighthouseFriends' list; the Marine keeper tables in the corpus (1900 to 1907) list 'Suthern, Edward W.' but were not matched to this station by column position, so they are not cited. Two Welch keepers appear; no source links them. Record checks: focal_height_m 18.0 and range 6 nm are not confirmed in any source read (the Coast Guard entry gives no height in the text read). The record's 'status: active' describes the skeleton-tower light; the 1909 tower is decommissioned. The 1909 tower dates and the 1851 keeper date are both used. No wreck or rescue at this light is named in any source read. Pre-1900 Canadian annual reports are not in the corpus. Parks Canada's own statement page (page_hl_eng.aspx?id=16453) returned a 404 or a blank shell, so the register text was taken from Heritage Guide. Fact-check 2026-10-27: the story now says the register calls the island both uninhabited and inhabited (its two passages differ); that LighthouseFriends' visitor information gives grounds open, tower closed and a view from South Point (the earlier 'no public access' line was wrong); that SaltWire (2025) gives the municipality's 2023 ownership; that the NSLPS lens history (5th order dioptric 1922 to 1941; 4th order 1992) is reported against LighthouseFriends' 1909 Chance lens; that the spindle reports spell the island 'Peters island' and place the reef in Grand passage, Digby county; that the spindle erection is in the Department's annual report dated December 1900 (the text read gives only the month and year of the report). The 1911 Sessional Paper table lists 'Peter island' among changes and improvements without a date in the text read, so the 1909 date rests on the register, LighthouseFriends and NSLPS. Wording: about nine LighthouseFriends passages were reworded under the copyright rule; government text (register, 1857 inspection, 1885 Sailing Directions, Marine reports) stays quoted with attribution.
